ThingDef.label: chewed timbers
ThingDef.description: The roof beams have been chewed from below until they are thin in the middle. Whatever did it took its time, and did not need light.

li.label: Judge the colony from the damage
li.successMessage: Two seasons of chewing, one brood, and the marks stop at chest height. That tells you roughly how many are in here and how big the largest gets. Nobody has to go through a door blind.
li.failMessage: Wood, holes, insects. You cannot put a number to it, and everyone guesses differently.

li.label: Work out why they settled here
li.successMessage: They came up through a capped cistern the builders forgot. The nest is thickest there, so the rooms above it are the ones to hold - and the corridor behind you is not a way out. You say so before anyone commits.
li.failMessage: You follow the damage in a circle and end up where you started.

ThingDef.label: spoor trail
ThingDef.description: A wet, dragged path across the flagstones, running one way more often than the other.

li.label: Follow it to the heart of the nest
li.successMessage: The trail is a routine: out for food, back to the brood, worn into a groove. You follow it the right way and reach the deep chamber knowing what is waiting there.
li.failMessage: You lose it on bare stone, find something that might be it, and lose that too.

li.label: Listen to the building instead
li.successMessage: You stop everyone and listen. Under the dripping there is a dry rattling two rooms east, and nothing at all to the west. Now you know which way to face.
li.failMessage: The building is full of running water and your own people breathing. You give it up.

ThingDef.label: ransom ledger
ThingDef.description: A tally book, kept better than anything else here: names, dates, amounts, and beside some names a second column.

li.label: Read what the second column means
li.successMessage: The second column is what they settled for. Every figure is lower than the asking price, and the gap widens down the page. This crew has been failing to get paid for a year and knows it - which changes how you talk to the man in charge.
li.failMessage: Numbers beside names, and they stay numbers beside names.

li.label: Trace whose seals these are
li.successMessage: Three of the seals on this page belong to houses that died out a century ago. The book was old before these bandits found it, and they simply kept writing in it. The guild will want to know who else has.
li.failMessage: Wax, pressed with something. You could not name one of them.

li.label: Take the page that names your rider
li.successMessage: One page out at the stitching and into your coat. Anyone who comes looking for this rider will find no record they were here.
li.failMessage: The stitching is tighter than it looks. The tear goes wide and loud, and the half with the name on it stays put.

ThingDef.label: drowned niche
ThingDef.description: A shrine niche cut into the wall at knee height, half under standing water. Something was left in it and never collected.

li.label: Read what was bound here
li.successMessage: It is a keeping-ward, and a good one - the niche was meant to hold something, not to protect it. You unpick the binding in the order it was made, which is the only order that does not wake it. The room feels larger afterwards.
li.failMessage: You get two turns into it before the pattern stops making sense, and you are fairly sure it noticed.

li.label: Finish the rite nobody came back to finish
li.successMessage: You do not know the words, so you use the ones you have, and you mean them. The company watches an eight-hundred-year-old errand finally get finished. Everyone walks out of the room lighter.
li.failMessage: You get about halfway before your voice gives away how little you know. Stopping there is worse than not starting.

li.label: Pocket what was left
li.successMessage: Offerings are for the dead, and the dead have never once come to collect. The silver goes into your coat, and nothing in the room says a word about it.
li.failMessage: Your hand closes on the silver and the room goes quiet in a way rooms should not. You put it back. It does not help.

ThingDef.label: traveler's cairn
ThingDef.description: Stones stacked with intent, weathered by years. People build these to mark something, or to keep something down, or to keep something safe. There is one way to find out which.

li.label: Shift the stones
li.successMessage: Stone by stone, and loudly. Under the last of them: a wrapped bundle somebody meant to come back for.
li.failMessage: The stack shifts wrong and settles deeper. Whatever is under there is under there for good now.

li.label: Read which stone bears the weight
li.successMessage: Every stack has one keystone, and whoever built this one wanted it findable. Two stones out, a reach in, and the cairn stands exactly as it stood.
li.failMessage: You pull the wrong stone and spend a bad moment holding up the rest with your forearm. The cairn keeps what it keeps.

ThingDef.label: trail journal
ThingDef.description: A travel journal in a waxed wrap, half under its owner. The last pages are the ones that matter, if they can still be read.

li.label: Work out where they were headed
li.successMessage: Water-stained, but the owner wrote like a surveyor: bearings, landmarks, days between them. The last entry names a place they never reached. You can find it.
li.failMessage: The wax held the rain out and the rot in. The pages that named names are a gray felt.

li.label: Read the writer, not the words
li.successMessage: Forget the smeared entries: look at what they packed, which page is worn from rereading, which map corner is soft from a thumb. They were going somewhere they had circled a long time. You know roughly where.
li.failMessage: A stranger's shorthand, a stranger's habits. Whatever they were chasing, they are done chasing it, and the journal keeps their counsel.
